Dow futures were up 1,100 points overnight. SpaceX and Tesla were down about 4%, and CoreWeave and Nebius were sliding. Same election, same night, same futures screen, and the market read it in two opposite directions.

I only have the headlines, but the split is easy to explain. Axios quoted someone calling it "an AI earthquake," and Business Insider ran a piece on data center votes at the ballot box. For months the AI buildout has been treated as a purely financial story: bond spreads, equity raises, who has the cash. Voters just reminded everyone it's also a land-use story. Data centers need power, zoning, and neighbors who don't mind the hum, and each of those is decided locally by people who vote. A cost of capital can now go up because of a county referendum, which doesn't fit neatly into anybody's model.

Meanwhile Fundstrat expects a post-midterm rally led by AI. Bloomberg's headline says gains are the weakest after midterm results like these. Both can't be right, and the confidence on each side is the thing I'd look at. After a week where Apple, Intel, and Amazon all disturbed the AI trade, "buy the tech dip" looks like a habit more than a view.

Ackman called the market "broken," which is the most useful thing anyone has said about it, mostly because he's still pitching Visa and Netflix right after. Broken, apparently, but not that broken.

I keep thinking about the investingLive question: what if good news for stocks becomes bad news for bonds? The ten-year only just dropped back near 5%.
